Self-service, standalone download sets you can download and run.

::: {.callout-important}
Tools here ingest or produce assessment data — a map of where a tenant is weak.
Treat that data as **Controlled**: keep it in-boundary, share only with
authorized personnel, and do not publish raw findings. Remediation guidance is
**advisory** — apply changes only through your normal change-control process.
:::

## Federal Application-Aware Networking Series

A **ten-volume, 58-book** program covering the network, identity, data-platform,
security-operations, governance, training, ServiceNow-automation, multi-cloud DDI and
day-2 architecture required for **FedRAMP Moderate** authorization under FedRAMP 20x
rules (mandatory January 1, 2027).

**[Read the series →](../customer-documents/federal-aan-series/Vol_0_Book_00a_FedAAN_Executive_Brief.qmd)**
— start with the two-page executive brief. Every book is browsable on this site and
carries a Word download button.

### Series structure

| Volume | Theme | Books |
|---|---|---|
| **Vol 0** | Executive Summary, Questionnaire & Control Crosswalk | 4 |
| **Vol I** | Foundation & Transport | 8 |
| **Vol II** | Data Platform | 4 |
| **Vol III** | Security Operations | 8 |
| **Vol IV** | Governance & Assurance | 7 |
| **Vol V** | Training & Certification | 5 |
| **Vol VI** | Implementation | 9 |
| **Vol VII** | ServiceNow Automation | 6 |
| **Vol VIII** | Multi-Cloud DDI | 1 |
| **Vol IX** | Day-2 Operations | 6 |
| **Total** | — | **58** |

A companion **Training Academy** (20 per-book courseware modules, 5 vendor labs,
and two tracks — compliance and implementation) is published alongside the series.

### Series requirements & roadmap

The program-level planning documents behind the series (kept in the repository
alongside the book sources):

| Document | Contents |
|---|---|
| [AAN Series Requirements (Word)](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/docs/customer-documents/federal-aan-series/AAN_Series_Requirements.docx) · [Markdown](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/docs/customer-documents/federal-aan-series/AAN_Series_Requirements.md) | Detailed requirements document for the whole program — functional requirements by volume group, integration matrix, NFRs, personas, KPIs |
| [ServiceNow Kit Expansion Roadmap](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/docs/customer-documents/federal-aan-series/AAN_ServiceNow_Kit_Expansion_Roadmap.md) | The kit portfolio and its sequencing — foundation kits (Vols VII–IX), the Identity & Access Governance Kit (Phase 2), and Phase 3+ candidates |

::: {.callout-note}
**Two editions, one source.** What you see here is the **federal edition**: written for
any federal agency, with no agency named. An **agency edition** renders from the same
source with an agency's own facts substituted — its enabling statute, namespace, tenant
and pre-filled tool inventory. That edition is not published: its facts live inside the
agency boundary, and the published tree cannot render it.
:::

| Download | Contents |
|---|---|
| [`aan-federal-series-latest.zip`](aan-federal-series-latest.zip) | The complete kit — every book as Word (`.docx`, per-volume folders) and PowerPoint (`.pptx`), plus the deployable operator kits: the ServiceNow day-2 catalog, the compliance scoped app, detection rules, the multi-cloud DDI landing-zone automation, and the training academy |
| [`federal-aan-series-bundle.docx`](../customer-documents/federal-aan-series/federal-aan-series-bundle.docx) | The whole series as one Word document — every book and academy page concatenated |

Both are **rebuilt from source on every deploy** — the `.docx` are the published
**federal** renders (no agency identity, no internal marking), so no fixed SHA-256
is published. The kit contains the federal edition only; the agency edition is not
distributed here.

## ScubaDrift

**Drift, exception-lifecycle, and continuous-monitoring gating on top of CISA
ScubaGear.** ScubaGear assesses a Microsoft 365 tenant against the CISA SCuBA
baselines; ScubaDrift adds the operational layer it leaves out — run-to-run
drift, risk-acceptance lifecycle, a continuous-monitoring gate, and remediation
**SLA aging** mapped to CISA BOD 25-01, NIST SP 800-137 (ISCM), NIST 800-53
CA-7, and FedRAMP ConMon. It stands on the sanctioned tool and never touches a
tenant — it reads ScubaGear's JSON output. Python 3.10+, zero runtime
dependencies.

| Download | Contents |
|---|---|
| [`scubadrift-latest.zip`](scubadrift-latest.zip) | Runnable package — source, 47-test suite, examples, figure sources, and `ScubaDrift-Documentation.docx` |
| [`ScubaDrift-Documentation.docx`](ScubaDrift-Documentation.docx) | The full documentation as a single Word document (also inside the zip) |

Quick start:

```bash
unzip scubadrift-latest.zip && cd scubadrift
pip install .            # or: pip install '.[yaml]'
scubadrift gate --results ScubaResults.json --exceptions exceptions.yaml
```

Both artifacts are **rebuilt on every deploy** from source (`tools/scubadrift/`),
so no fixed SHA-256 is published here. A versioned archive
(`scubadrift-<version>.zip`) is published alongside the `-latest` alias.

## Verifying a download

```powershell
Get-FileHash .\download.zip -Algorithm SHA256
# compare the output to the SHA-256 listed above before running
# then run the bundled test suite (where applicable):
#   pip install '.[dev]' ; pytest -q
```
